A terrestrial [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="OSAVC31" /> located in the [[Indoumodo system/Legends|Indoumodo system]] of [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]],<ref name="TEA" /> '''Indoumodo''' was a lush world<ref name="AOR" /> with [[Jungle/Legends|jungles]] and [[Forest/Legends|forests]] that were [[Homeworld/Legends|home]] to [[Kouhun/Legends|kouhuns]],<ref name="OSAVC31" /> [[Poison/Legends|poisonous]] [[Arthropod/Legends|arthropods]] that dwelled in [[Water/Legends|damp]] [[Cave/Legends|caves]] and passages underground.<ref name="Figurine" /> The creatures were also known to dwell in vast, hollow [[Tree/Legends|trees]] and hunted [[Dog/Legends|dog]]-sized creatures that lived in the trees' crevices.<ref name="TOTG" /> Located near the end of the [[Corellian Run/Legends|Corellian Run]], Indoumodo was a destination for [[Assassin/Legends|assassins]] and poisoners who would venture to capture the kouhuns for use as untraceable [[Death/Legends|killers]].<ref name="AOR" />

Shortly before the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|outbreak]] of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]],<ref name="Date">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates the events of [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']], and thus the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|start]] of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] and the [[Plot to assassinate Senator Amidala/Legends|assassination attempt]] on [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]], to [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]].</ref> the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]] tasked fellow [[Hunting/Legends|hunter]] [[Zam Wesell/Legends|Zam Wesell]] with using a pair of starved kouhuns from Indoumodo to [[Plot to assassinate Senator Amidala/Legends|assassinate]] [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. The assassination was a failure, as both kouhuns were killed by [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]].<ref name="WMAM?">''[[Star Wars: What Makes a Monster?]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Indoumodo was introduced via mention in the [[2002]] reference book ''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones: The Visual Dictionary]]'', written by [[David West Reynolds (real person)|David West Reynolds]].<ref name="TVD">''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> The planet received a visual depiction in the reference title ''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]'', written by [[Ann Margaret Lewis (real person)|Ann Margaret Lewis]]<ref name="TNEGTAS">''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''</ref> and released on [[October 31]], [[2006]].<ref name="Penguin-Paperback">{{PenguinRandomHouse|url=books/100839/star-wars-the-new-essential-guide-to-alien-species-by-ann-margaret-lewis-and-helen-keier/9780345477606|text=Star Wars: The New Essential Guide to Alien Species}} {{C|Paperback}}</ref> The [[2009]] book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' placed the Indoumodo [[Star system/Legends|system]], and thus Indoumodo, in grid square S-18.<ref name="TEA" />

In contrast to other sources, the ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Revised Core Rulebook]]'', a 2002 rulebook for the ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]'' from [[Wizards of the Coast]], claims that the homeworld of the kouhuns is unknown.<ref name="RGRCR">''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Revised Core Rulebook]]''</ref> The [[Star Wars: The Official Figurine Collection 48|forty-eighth issue]] of ''[[Star Wars: The Official Figurine Collection]]'',<ref name="Figurine" /> released around [[November 21]], 2006,<ref name="Date2">{{OFCdates|48}}</ref> misspells the planet's name as "Induomodo."<ref name="Figurine" />
